qc/runs/coldwater-strict-2026-10-08-v16-full/raw-evidence-index.json (all 19 artifact hashes re-verified on LF-normalised bytes: all match) and the three v15 hosted verifier/reward.json files it cites
evidence: Reward arrangement does not invert the ranking. tests/scoring.toml (gates render=0.0, constraints=0.0; weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2; floors functional 0.05) and tests/tools/score.py are byte-identical to the frozen template (template-controlled, not editable); function carries 0.6 vs 0.4 for craft, gates carry no mass (score.py:41-48 zeroes reward on a failed gate or floor). Gates only test public hard requirements a stronger app must also meet: render = workspace loads/reloads; constraints = own-drawn editor surface (ui.md:3, policy.md:3) and a saved snippet surviving storage clear + reload (integration.md:7-9, behaviour.md:9) -- the policy-mandated 'convincing dead app' exclusion, with lenient wording (any success sign, typing or paste, catcher input allowed, no route/selector assumptions). Functional criteria (43, weight 59) each have a positive control before negatives (functional/prompt.md:16; e.g. cw_dynamic_code_refused harmless-draft control, cw_stop_cancels_pending_work control marker, cw_stale_save_refused/keeps_draft require A's save to succeed and B refused, cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state and cw_newer_revision_notice_keeps_draft fail if live refresh never happens), so a dead feature cannot earn credit that a working one would lose; void-attempt rules prevent timing races from penalising a correct app; app_context.md:32 keeps Run-independent criteria scorable. Polish criteria all require working features (Format/Undo/Redo/Replace all/Save focus return, undo/redo disabled states, unsaved marker), so polish does not reward a dead shell; visual is likert 0-5 with anchors and capped at 0.2. Worst-case probe: a styled shell passing both gates plus ~3 functional weight units (0.0508 > floor) with polish 0.5 and visual 1.0 scores about 0.33, still below a plain app at functional 0.5 / polish 0.33 / visual 0.4 (~0.45); only an app that fails every polish criterion with minimum visual could fall below such a shell, which is the template's 0.6/0.2/0.2 policy trade-off, not a task-authored inversion. Minor bounded asymmetry (Note-level, not a defect): cw_controls_keyboard_and_focus excuses absent controls, so an app missing Format/Find/Replace keeps up to 1/6 of polish (<=0.033 reward) that a fuller app with one unfocusable control loses, but the missing features cost more in functional (Format alone: 4.5/59*0.6 = 0.046) and in cw_focus_returns_to_code/cw_controls_feedback_and_labels, so net order is preserved. Measured ordering exists only for v15 bytes (same golden, different brief/app_context/functional criteria): Oracle 1.0 > GPT-5.6-luna 0.5746 (F 0.4576, P 1.0, V 0.5) > nop 0.0, hashes verified. Risk stays true: no configured-judge run and no reward-ordering record with mutated weak apps exists on these v16 bytes (raw-evidence-index scope says so), so monotonicity is established structurally only; also the v15 audit notes the judge over-passed 4 criteria worth 6.0/59, which is judge noise that could locally reorder close candidates.
